body.goals: Medium-term capital growth over a 2-3 year horizon. Diversified across sectors, countries and risk tiers (core, growth, speculative); every position is justified by a written thesis built from news, fundamentals and deep research. Because the horizon is short, capital preservation matters: avoid deep drawdowns and do not rely on a long recovery period, since a deep drawdown may not recover within 2-3 years.
body.notes:
STRATEGY PRINCIPLES
1. Diversification is enforced by caps, not target weights: max 10% per position, 35% per sector, 70% per country, at least 8 positions, cash 5% (max 20%).
2. Every holding carries exactly one risk tier (dimension 'risk'), assigned by these criteria in this order. SPECULATIVE if ANY applies: market cap below USD 2 bn, OR annualised volatility above 35%, OR not yet profitable / under 3 years of profitable history. CORE only if ALL apply: market cap above USD 10 bn, AND annualised volatility at or below 25%, AND profitable for 5+ years. GROWTH is everything else. Reclassify at the thesis review date or when a criterion changes. Tier limits: core at least 40% of the portfolio, growth at most 45%, speculative at most 15%.
3. No buy without a thesis. The thesis must be built from recent news, fundamentals and deep research, and must state why it is owned, its KPIs, and its exit conditions.
4. Trades are driven by fundamentals and events only. A price move alone is never a reason to buy or sell.
5. Review or exit triggers: a thesis KPI breach, a severity-3 news event (guidance cut, M&A, dividend cut), or a thesis review date that has passed.
6. Risk limits (strategy `risk`): portfolio volatility at most 20% a year, a position down 25% or more from cost needs a thesis review, no single company above 10% counting ETF holdings, portfolio drawdown from its 1-year peak at most 20%, and no two holdings with return correlation above 0.85 that together weigh 10% or more. A risk-limit breach only forces a review of the thesis; it is never a sell signal on its own.
7. Propose new ideas so that they fill under-represented sectors, countries or risk tiers rather than adding to concentrations.
8. Currency: no cap on foreign-currency exposure (a deliberate choice; base currency is CZK).
9. A position above the 10% cap is judged on its projected outlook, not on size alone. If the thesis and deep research still project further growth (KPIs on track, valuation leaves upside), hold it, add nothing, and let deposits and other positions dilute it; re-check at each review. If the projected growth is exhausted or the thesis is weakened, trim it back to 8%. Backstop (proposed, edit if unwanted): a position above 15% is trimmed to 10% regardless of outlook.
10. New deposits go first to the most under-represented risk tier, sector or country, and within it to positions with the strongest projected growth and an intact thesis. Do not deposit into a position already above its cap.
11. Horizon is 2-3 years: prefer positions whose thesis pays off within that window, and treat any thesis needing longer than 3 years to play out as speculative.
12. News and thesis triggers that force a review of the position (never an automatic sale): the thesis requirements for holding are no longer met (a quarterly report misses the thesis KPIs or expectations), a guidance cut or profit warning, M&A involving the company, a dividend cut or suspension, and regulatory or legal action (escalated when it bears on the thesis).
13. Thesis review cadence: core and growth every 3 months, speculative monthly; every thesis is also re-checked after each quarterly report and after any event in rule 12.
14. When the portfolio drawdown limit (20%) is hit: freeze all new buys and review every thesis; buying resumes only for positions whose thesis is re-confirmed and once the drawdown is back under the limit.
15. Buying rules: (a) instruments are plain stocks and unleveraged ETFs only, no leveraged, inverse or derivative products; (b) a new position starts at no more than 5% (core), 3% (growth) or 1.5% (speculative) of the portfolio and may grow afterwards within the caps (starting sizes proposed, edit if unwanted); (c) valuation gate: do not buy when the deep research shows the stock is clearly overvalued on its valuation methods.
16. No glide path is set for the end of the horizon; the owner decides manually when it approaches.

rules.description: No single stock above 10% of the portfolio.
